query_1: Through which side is the breath drawn in and through which released in this practice?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Having drawn the breath in through one side, one should hold it under firm restraint and then release it slowly through the other, never forcibly.
query_1: Should the breath be let out quickly or gradually?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The alternating method is set out: drawing in through the left and releasing through the right, then drawing in through the right and releasing through the left; practised constantly in this way, the channels of the restrained become pure after three months.
query_1: How is the alternating channel practice to be carried out over time?
notes: gloss corrected: gloss was missing the result clause (purification of the channels after three months), which query_1 asks about

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: One should release the breath in due measure, fill in due measure, and hold in due measure; in this way attainment is reached.
query_1: What does keeping each phase of the breath measured accomplish?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The nasal cleansing purifies the skull, grants clear sight, and quickly destroys the mass of diseases arising above the collarbone.
query_1: Which cleansing practice clears the head and improves eyesight?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Fixed gazing frees one from eye disorders and bolts the door against sloth; it should be guarded as carefully as a box of gold.
query_1: Which practice is said to cure eye ailments and drive off drowsiness?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: When the breath moves in the central channel, steadiness of mind arises; that condition of firm mind is itself the state beyond mind.
query_1: What state of mind arises when the breath moves in the central channel?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Closing the mouth and drawing the air in slowly through both channels, so that it is felt with a sound from throat down to heart.
query_1: Which breathing method produces a sound felt from the throat to the heart?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The essence of the body becomes free of every disorder; by this method the foremost practitioner truly prospers on earth.
query_1: What is claimed about the body of one who follows this method?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Having bound the lotus posture properly, with neck and abdomen held straight, closing the mouth, one should expel the breath through the nose with effort.
query_1: How should one sit and expel the breath in this practice?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: One should move the breath within one's own body by will; when fatigue arises in the body, one should then fill through the right.
query_1: What should be done when tiredness sets in during breath practice?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: At the end of the inhalation, binding the chin lock firmly, one should exhale slowly; this is the swooning practice, which pleases by making the mind faint.
query_1: Which practice uses a chin lock and produces a pleasant faintness of mind?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The inverted action, the ascending practice and the stirring of the coiled energy complete the set of ten seals, which destroy old age and death.
query_1: How many seals are listed altogether, and what are they said to destroy?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Declared by the primal lord, divine, granting the eight powers, dear to all the adepts and hard to obtain even for the gods.
query_1: How difficult are these practices said to be to obtain?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Applying the throat lock, one should hold the breath upward; as a snake struck with a stick becomes straight like a stick.
query_1: What comparison with a snake describes the effect of the throat lock?
notes: verse ends mid-simile; what becomes straight (the coiled energy) is stated in the next verse

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: One who becomes steady with the tongue turned upward and drinks the nectar conquers death within half a month, without doubt.
query_1: What is claimed for the practice of turning the tongue upward?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The fluid said to flow constantly from the palate is described as salty, pungent and sour, resembling milk, and comparable to honey and clarified butter; it removes disease and ends old age.
query_1: Which tastes are attributed to the fluid said to flow from the palate?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The essence flows down from the moon at the crown, and by that flowing away death comes to people.
query_1: Why is the downward flow of this essence said to bring about death?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The cavity that generates knowledge, joined with five streams, is where the space-moving seal is established, in that untainted void.
query_1: Where is the seal that moves in space said to be established?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: One seed of creation, one seal, one self-supported deity, one state beyond mind.
query_1: Which single seed, seal, deity and state are named together?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The upward-flying lock is so called by practitioners because, when it is bound, the breath flies up in the central channel.
query_1: Why is this abdominal lock named after upward flight?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: One should draw in above and below the navel with effort; practising for six months, one conquers death without doubt.
query_1: How long must the abdominal drawing-in be practised, according to the claim made?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Of all the locks the upward-flying one is the best; when it is firmly bound, liberation happens of its own accord.
query_1: Which of the locks is called the best, and what follows from mastering it?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: When the downward breath is made to rise and reaches the region of fire, the flame grows long, fanned by the wind.
query_1: What happens to the inner fire when the downward breath is drawn upward?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: By this very method the breath comes to dissolution; from then on death, old age, disease and the like do not arise.
query_1: What is claimed to follow once the breath dissolves by this method?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: These three locks are the best, practised by the great adepts, and practitioners know them to be the means of accomplishing all the teachings of this system.
query_1: How are the three locks regarded in relation to the system as a whole?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: A technical description of the ascending practice, in which the vital essence is drawn upward and retained rather than lost.
query_1: What does the practice of drawing the vital essence upward involve?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The vital essence depends on the mind and life depends on that essence; therefore both the essence and the mind should be carefully guarded.
query_1: How are mind, vital essence and life said to depend on one another?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: In this practice the first portion is discarded as too bilious and the last as without essence; the cool middle portion is what is used.
query_1: Which portion is used and which discarded in this practice?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: If a woman preserves her own essence through skilled practice of the ascending technique, she too is an accomplished practitioner.
query_1: Is this practice described as available to women as well as men?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: In the thunderbolt seat one should hold the feet firmly with the hands and press the bulb at the place near the ankles.
query_1: How are the hands and feet positioned in this energy-stirring practice?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The entire method of the breath should be practised together with the mind; elsewhere the thoughtful person should not let mental activity operate.
query_1: Should breath practice be done with the mind engaged or disengaged?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Now the excellent method of absorption will be declared: destroyer of death, an easy means, and producing the highest bliss.
query_1: What is introduced as an easy means that destroys death?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Who truly knows the greatness of the royal path? Knowledge, liberation, stability and attainment are obtained through the teacher's word.
query_1: Through what are knowledge, liberation and attainment said to be obtained?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: When the breath flows in the central channel and the mind enters the void, then the knower uproots all actions.
query_1: What becomes of accumulated actions when the breath enters the central channel?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Salutation to you, the deathless one; even time itself has been conquered by you, into whose mouth this whole moving and unmoving world has fallen.
query_1: Who is saluted as having conquered time itself?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Since the breath has become familiar, having awakened the coiled energy together with the fire, it should enter the central channel without obstruction.
query_1: What must be awakened before the breath can enter the central channel?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The mind is lord of the senses, the breath is lord of the mind, dissolution is lord of the breath, and that dissolution rests upon the inner sound.
query_1: What is the chain of mastery running from the senses to the inner sound?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: With all intentions cut off and every activity exhausted, a dissolution arises that is knowable only to oneself and beyond the reach of speech.
query_1: How is the state of dissolution described in terms of being expressible?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: They keep saying dissolution, but what is its mark? It is the forgetting of objects, because latent tendencies do not rise again.
query_1: What is the defining mark of dissolution?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Through the difference of state and location between the auspicious seal and the space-moving seal, the bliss of mental dissolution arises in the void whose nature is the happiness of consciousness.
query_1: What produces the bliss of mental dissolution?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: With the eyes half open, the mind steady, the gaze fixed at the tip of the nose, dissolving both sun and moon, motionless, one beholds the supreme luminous seed of all.
query_1: How are the eyes and the gaze held in this meditation?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Between the sun and the moon, in the unsupported space, established in the wheel of the sky, is the seal named after moving in space.
query_1: Where is the seal located that takes its name from moving in space?
notes: meaning ok; devanagari has a scribal typo सूर्च्या for सूर्या (sūryā)

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: One should not dwell on external things nor on internal ones; abandoning all thought, one should think of nothing whatsoever.
query_1: What should the mind attend to, whether outside or within?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: In the third stage a sound like a kettledrum is recognised in the space; then one goes to the great void, the resting place of all attainments.
query_1: Which sound marks the third stage, and where does it lead?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: In the final stage, when the breath has pierced the knot and reached the seat, a flute-like sound arises, resonant as a plucked vina.
query_1: Which instrument's sound marks the culminating stage?
notes: gloss corrected: verse names both the flute (vaiṇava) and the vina resonance; gloss said only lute

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: As a bee drinking nectar has no regard for the scent, so the mind absorbed in the inner sound has no longing for objects.
query_1: What comparison with a bee explains absorption in the inner sound?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: Abandoning all thought and with a careful mind, one who desires mastery in this discipline should attend to the inner sound alone.
query_1: What should one attend to exclusively when seeking mastery?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: The practitioner joined in absorption knows neither smell, taste, form, touch nor sound, and knows neither self nor other.
query_1: What does the practitioner in deep absorption cease to perceive?

title: Hatha Yoga Pradipika
gloss_en: He knows neither cold nor heat, neither pain nor pleasure, and neither honour nor dishonour.
query_1: Which pairs of opposites stop registering in deep absorption?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Misconception is false knowledge that is not founded on the actual form of its object.
query_1: What is it called when the mind holds a belief that does not match what is actually there?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Memory is the retention of an object previously experienced, without its being lost.
query_1: How is remembering defined among the movements of the mind?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Practice is the sustained effort to remain established in that steady state.
query_1: What exactly is meant by effort directed at staying steady?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: For those absorbed into matter and those without bodies, that state arises from birth itself.
query_1: How do beings without physical bodies come to that absorbed condition?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: For others it is preceded by conviction, energy, memory, absorption and discernment.
query_1: Which five qualities must come first for ordinary practitioners?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: From that follows the attainment of inward-turned awareness and also the disappearance of obstacles.
query_1: What two results follow from the practice just described?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Engrossment that is still mixed with word, meaning and idea is the deliberative kind.
query_1: Which meditative absorption is still entangled with language and concepts?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: On attaining clarity in the reflection-free state, inner serenity arises.
query_1: What arises once the subtlest reflective state becomes clear?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: The cause of what is to be avoided is the conjunction of the seer with the seen.
query_1: What is the root cause of the suffering that can still be prevented?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: The seer is pure seeing alone; though pure, it looks on by way of mental concepts.
query_1: How is the pure witness described in relation to what it perceives?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Unrestricted by class, place, time or circumstance, these restraints become universal, the great vow.
query_1: When do the ethical restraints become universal rather than conditional?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: When truthfulness is firmly established, the practitioner becomes the ground of actions and their results, so that what is spoken comes to pass.
query_1: What capacity comes from being firmly grounded in truthfulness?
notes: gloss corrected: āśrayatva belongs to the practitioner, not to truthfulness; gloss reworded

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: When non-stealing is firmly established, all riches present themselves.
query_1: What follows from becoming firmly settled in not taking what belongs to others?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: From cleanliness comes distaste for one's own body and disinclination to contact with others.
query_1: What attitude toward the body results from purity?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Attainment of absorption comes from surrender to the lord.
query_1: What is gained by devoting oneself entirely to the divine?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: That being established, the regulation of breath is the interruption of the movement of inhalation and exhalation.
query_1: How is breath control defined once the posture is steady?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: The three together, applied to a single object, constitute complete integration.
query_1: What is the name for concentration, meditation and absorption practised as one?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: The mind's calm and steady flow comes about through the impression left by that restraint.
query_1: What makes the mind's tranquil flow become continuous?
notes: gloss corrected: saṃskāra here is the impression of nirodha from the preceding sutra, not habitual impressions generally

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: The substratum is that which persists through its properties, whether subsided, presently arisen, or not yet manifest.
query_1: How is the underlying substance related to past, present and future characteristics?
notes: gloss corrected: śānta rendered as 'subsided/past' rather than 'latent'

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: By focusing on strengths one obtains the strength of an elephant and the like.
query_1: How does one acquire great physical power through focused attention?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Experience arises from failing to distinguish two utterly distinct things, since one exists for the sake of the other; from focusing on what exists for its own sake comes knowledge of the self.
query_1: How does knowledge of the true self arise, given that experience depends on a confusion?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: From focusing on the gross form, essential nature, subtlety, interconnection and purpose of the elements comes mastery over them.
query_1: What five aspects must be focused on to gain mastery over the physical elements?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: From focusing on the process of perception, its essential nature, the sense of self, interconnection and purpose comes mastery over the senses.
query_1: What five aspects must be focused on to gain mastery over the faculties of perception?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: When the purity of the intellect equals that of the self, there is liberation.
query_1: What condition of equality between intellect and self brings liberation?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Transformation into another kind of existence comes about through the filling in of nature.
query_1: How is a change from one form of existence into another brought about?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: An object is known or unknown according to whether it colours the mind.
query_1: What determines whether a given object is known or remains unknown?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: The mind coloured by both the seer and the seen apprehends everything.
query_1: Why is the mind able to apprehend all objects?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: The removal of these is described in the same way as the removal of the afflictions.
query_1: How is the removal of these accomplished, according to what was said earlier?

title: Patanjali Yoga Sutras
gloss_en: Sequence corresponds to moments and is grasped at the end of a transformation.
query_1: How is succession related to moments, and when is it apprehended?
